approvedDeviation: #825 rebase onto #828: packages/vault/src/schema/atlas-census.ts stops COUNT(*) of share.grant/share.fulfillment on Atlas first paint so the SQL budget stays 140; export completeness is unchanged (tables still registered and still carried). Prior: #825 Wave 1: the grant plane becomes first-class in the vault. schema/share-grant.ts adds two NEW STRICT tables — `share_grant` (audience_kind/audience_id, subject_type/subject_id, capability view|edit, granted_at/revoked_at, granted_by, max_size_bytes, with a partial UNIQUE index enforcing one live grant per audience x subject) and `share_fulfillment` (grant_id, peer_vault_id, state awaiting_channel|syncing|delivered|remove_sent|removed, updated_at, detail). A share is now a STANDING GRANT — meaning — and delivery is per-audience-vault state held apart from it, so "who may see this" no longer depends on whether a transport succeeded. Both are registered in schema/tables.ts as share.grant and share.fulfillment, so the canonical walk (listVaultEntities, per the #724 W5 note) carries them with no adapter and no content bytes: a granted subject's bytes are already covered by the content walk through the subject's own tables. Both MUST be carried. Dropping share_grant would hand back a restored vault that had forgotten every share it ever made while the projected rows in audience vaults kept existing; dropping share_fulfillment would make it believe nothing had ever been delivered, re-sending every subject and unable to tell an acknowledged revocation from one still in flight. share_grant's polymorphic (subject_type, subject_id) pair is registered in POLY_REF_EXCLUSIONS beside share_circle_grant's container pair and for the same reason: durable share control truth, ended by a dated revocation rather than swept as a dangling pointer. Nothing is dropped or renamed — share_circle_grant and the whole commons plane are untouched, because commons is now the edit-fulfillment strategy under the grant plane rather than a rival record of the same fact. The change adds rung three to VAULT_MIGRATIONS: an IF NOT EXISTS create (a no-op on fresh files, which get the tables from the baseline composition after SHARE_COMMONS_DDL) plus a pure-SQL backfill that restates live commons grants — named circles with a uniform capability and no refused member stay one circle-audience grant; implicit circles, capability-variant circles, and circles containing a refusal decompose per party (a circle row over a roster with a refused party would keep reaching them); refused members get no grant, and the limit case — a live grant every member refused — deliberately migrates to nothing while the commons row and the refusals survive as the record; and fulfillment state is derived from the live party/vault bindings and per-member commons status. The backfill only reads the commons tables and only writes the two new ones, carries every timestamp from its source row, and mints ids in SQL, so it is deterministic and vault-preserving. Export completeness re-audited in packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts.
